output.brief:
August's dip is almost entirely a cooling failure on floors 6 to 8. The east chiller failed on 4 August and wasn't repaired until 19 August; rooms ran at 26 to 29°C. Guests there rated room comfort 6.1 (down from 8.4); checkouts after the repair were back to normal. Floors 1 to 5 barely moved. Without the outage, August would have been about 8.5. Extra desk complaints are nearly all room temperature (1 to 24).

Housekeeping and kiosks don't explain it: cleanliness and check-in scores are flat, in-house inspection pass rates are flat, and kiosk complaints and queue times fell. The survey itself didn't change. The 6% rate rise may have nudged value-for-money, but it can't be separated from the usual August dip.

Confidence: high on the cooling cause, moderate on the rate question.

Next: don't give notice to Orrin, pull the kiosks, reverse the rate rise yet, or drop the floors 6 to 8 responses from the score (that would hide a real failure while the score affects bonuses). Restore the deferred maintenance on both chillers, stock critical spares, and write a cooling-outage guest-recovery procedure. Keep watching value scores.
